comments.body_html:
Take a look at https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/enum/

I think that, to be compliant, you need to preserve unknown integers. But, if you do that, you'll need to change the ProtoEnum definition and the code generation for ProtoEnum subclasses to preserve the field numbers.

The ProtoJSON description doesn't really say what to do if the string/integer values don't map to existing values.

When using actual APIs, do we every receive

I think that this is the Java parsing implementation:
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/2f21136f4ea05813a4e2cffd4ab6337a5a09cecb/java/util/src/main/java/com/google/protobuf/util/JsonFormat.java#L2448

Maybe we need to set ;enum-encoding=int in the request to get any benefit from the unknown enum value behavior?

@Yusufihsangorgel I think that this is likely a big project that you'll have to research a bit before you take it on.

comments.body_html:
For proto3 the conformance suite requires an unknown integer to round-trip as a number (EnumFieldUnknownValue). By default Java's JsonFormat and Go's protojson print integers only for unknown values. Without enum-encoding=int, Showcase GetEnum can return one, and the Dart client throws on it today. Dart already keeps unknown names, so asking for integers can come later.

I'd generate the value numbers, map known integers to constants, keep unknown ones and accept 0 for NullValue. Should ProtoEnum get a nullable number, or would a Rust-style unknown variant fit better?

comments.body:
For proto3 the conformance suite requires an unknown integer to round-trip as a number ([EnumFieldUnknownValue][1]). By default Java's [JsonFormat][2] and Go's [protojson][3] print integers only for unknown values. Without `enum-encoding=int`, Showcase [GetEnum][4] can return one, and the Dart client throws on it today. Dart already keeps unknown names, so asking for integers can come later.

I'd generate the value numbers, map known integers to constants, keep unknown ones and accept 0 for NullValue. Should `ProtoEnum` get a nullable number, or would a [Rust-style unknown variant][5] fit better?

[1]: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/2f21136f4ea05813a4e2cffd4ab6337a5a09cecb/conformance/binary_json_conformance_suite.cc#L3278-L3286
[2]: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/2f21136f4ea05813a4e2cffd4ab6337a5a09cecb/java/util/src/main/java/com/google/protobuf/util/JsonFormat.java#L1556-L1557
[3]: https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf-go/blob/3933e752f9ea536e2cf45bf15b321274293863d3/encoding/protojson/encode.go#L331-L333
[4]: https://github.com/googleapis/gapic-showcase/blob/c804ae4fb988f92e54ddf5a6c816c61e9e62e98e/server/services/compliance_service.go#L135-L158
[5]: https://github.com/googleapis/google-cloud-rust/blob/16628efbcde33ee1d62f7ee68a833c9ea8dae13f/src/generated/cloud/workflows/v1/src/model.rs#L666-L678

comments.body_html:
I’d propose nullable number and string members, with declared constants carrying both. Unknown integer values in ordinary open enums use JSON numbers and decimal-string query values. This breaks the existing string-only API. Unknown-name decoding remains outside this representation sketch.

final int? number;
final String? value;
const State._(this.number, this.value);
static const ready = State._(1, 'READY'), unknown = State._(123, null);
Object? toJson() => value ?? number;
String toQueryValue() => value ?? number!.toString();
